questions.explanation_english: Optical fiber is a technology used to transmit data by sending short light pulses along a long fiber which is typically made of glass or plastic.  Total internal reflection of light is used in the fiber optical cable. This effect is used in optical fibres to confine light in the core. Light travel through the fibre core, bouncing back and forth off the boundary between the core and cladding.  Cladding is the outer optical material surrounding the core having reflecting index lower than core. It helps to keep the light within the core throughout the phenomena of total internal reflection.

questions.explanation_english: The metastable state is the state which lies between the ground state and excited state. The atom in the ground state absorbs some energy and goes to the excited state. From an excited state, it loses some energy and comes to a metastable state. The lifetime of the metastable state is 10–3 sec.  A metastable state is one which has a mean life time of the order of 10–3 s or more (much larger than 10–8 s). Some atomic systems such as chromium neon etc. posses metastable states.

questions.question_english: In a photoelectric effect experiment at a frequency above cut off, the number of electrons ejected is proportional to
questions.question_hindi: प्रकाश विद्युत परिणाम प्रयोग में विगलन ऊपर वाली आवृत्ति में निष्कासित किये गये इलेक्ट्रान की संख्या इससे समानुपाती होती है
options_english: the frequency of the incident light
questions.explanation_english: The photoelectric effect is the phenomenon where electrons are emitted from a material when it is exposed to light.  The photoelectric effect does not occur at all if the frequency of the light source is below a certain value. This value which is characteristic of the kind of metal surface used in the experiment, is called cutoff frequency. Above the cutoff frequency each photon of light carries, sufficient energy to eject an electron. Since each photon can eject one electron, increasing the intensity of light increases the number of photon reaching the material's surface and consequently increases the number of electrons ejected. So, the number of electron ejected in the photoelectric effect is directly proportional to the intensity of light.

questions.question_english: Thermocouple consists of
questions.question_hindi: तापयुग्म में होता है
questions.explanation_english: A thermocouple is a temperature sensor that operates based on the principle of the seebeck effect. It is a device composed of two dissimilar metal wires or conductors that are joined together at one end to form a junction. The other ends of the wires are typically connected to a measuring instrument or a control system.  When there is a temperature difference between the two junctions of a thermocouple, it generates a voltage known as the thermoelectric voltage. It is directly proportional to the temperature difference between the two junctions. By measuring this voltage, the temperature at one of the junctions (known as measurement or hot junction) can be inferred relative to the temperature at the other junction (known as the reference of cold junction).

questions.explanation_english: A superconductors is defined as a substance that offers no resistance to the electric current when it becomes colder than a critical temperature. For example – aluminum, copper oxide, magnesium diboride etc.  When a superconductor is cooled below its critical temperature, it forms cooper pairs - a quantum mechanical phenomenon involving pairs of electrons with opposite momentum and spin. These cooper pairs in addition to zero electrical resistance also generate a perfect cancellation of any external magnetic field within the superconductors. As a result a super conductor exhibits strong diamagnetic properties, actively expelling magnetic field from its interior.

questions.explanation_english: In superconductors, the energy gap is primarily due to interaction between electron and lattice vibrations which are known as phonons. This interaction is referred to as the electron phonon interaction. These interactions lead to the formation of pairs of electrons called cooper pairs with opposite momentum and spin.  The energy gap in a superconductor refers to the energy difference between the highest filled electron state (located below the gap) and the lowest available empty state (located above the gap) in the superconducting energy spectrum.  This energy gap is a characteristic feature of superconductors and is responsible for their unique properties such as zero electrical resistance and the expulsion of magnetic fields (Meissner effect).

questions.question_english: A diode that has a negative resistance characteristic is the
questions.question_hindi: ऋणात्मक प्रतिरोध विशेषतावाला डायोड होता है
questions.explanation_english: A tunnel diode (also known as Esaki diode) is a type of semiconductor diode that has negative resistance due to the quantum mechanical effect called tunneling. This feature (negative resistance) makes it useful in oscillator and microwave amplifier applications.  Tunnel diodes are constructed with germanium or gallium arsenide by doping the p and n regions much more heavily than in a conventional rectifier diode. options_english: Observed only in atoms with an even number of electrons
Observed only in atoms with an odd number of electrons

questions.explanation_english: Normal Zeeman effect is the phenomenon that explains the splitting of a spectral line into three components in a magnetic field when observed in a direction perpendicular to the applied magnetic field.  Normal Zeeman effect can be seen in atoms having zero spin. If there are even number of electrons in the valance shell, they should pair off and their magnetic moments get cancelled. So, they act like spinless (S = O) particles. Hence for normal Zeeman effect to occur, valance electrons of the atom must be even.

questions.explanation_english: The resistivity of conductor increases with increasing temperature. The increase is not very large and is typically proportional to temperature T. According to, ( ) o 1 T ρ = ρ + α∆ Where α is temperature coefficient of resistivity  The temperature coefficient of resistivity is negative for semiconductor. This means that the resistivity decreases as we raise the temperature of such a material. The magnitude of the temperature coefficient of resistivity is often quite large for a semiconducting material. This fact is used to construct thermometers to detect small changes in temperature. Such a device is called a thermistor.

questions.explanation_english: Beta decay is a form of radioactive decay that occurs when a nucleus emits a beta particle, which is either an electron or a position. It occurs when there is an imbalance between the number of neutrons and protons in the nucleus of an atom. Then nucleus becomes unstable and emits a beta particle to regain stability.  Beta decay conserves iso-spain, Baryon number and charge.  Parity refers to the concept of spatial symmetry. It describes whether a system remains unchanged under spatial inversion. Which is the transformation of coordinates from (x, y, z) to (-x, -y, -z). While parity is conserved in many fundamental interactions such as electromagnetic interaction, it is not conserved in weak interactions which are responsible for certain types of particle decay (β).

questions.question_hindi: कमरे का तापमान पर आन्तरिक अर्धचालक में होने वाले करेंट का कारण है
questions.explanation_english: Intrinsic Semiconductor – A semiconductor in an extremely pure form is known as intrinsic semiconductor. In an intrinsic semiconductor, even at rooms temperature, hole-electron pairs are created. When electric field is applied across an intrinsic semiconductor, the current conduction takes place by two processes namely by free electrons and holes.  The free electrons are produced due to the breaking up of some covalent bonds by thermal energy. At the same time holes are created in the covalent bonds. Under the influence of electric field, conduction through the semiconductor is by both free electrons and holes. Therefore, the total current inside the semiconductor is the sum of currents due to free electrons and holes.

questions.explanation_english: A Geiger Muller counter is a device used for the detection and measurement of ionizing radiation.  When ionizing radiation enters the GM tube, it ionizes gas atoms or molecules within the tube creating free charge carriers (positive ions and electrons). These free charge carriers are then accelerated by a high voltage applied across the detector, leading to further ionization events and the creation of more charge carriers. This process results in a detectable electrical pulse or discharge, which is recorded and used to determine the presence and intensity of the radiation. questions.explanation_english: Optical fiber is a technology used to transmit data by sending short light pulses along a long fiber which is typically made of glass or plastic.  Total internal reflection of light is used in the fiber optical cable. This effect is used in optical fibres to confine light in the core. Light travel through the fibre core, bouncing back and forth off the boundary between the core and cladding.  Cladding is the outer optical material surrounding the core having reflecting index lower than core. It helps to keep the light within the core throughout the phenomena of total internal reflection.

questions.explanation_english: The metastable state is the state which lies between the ground state and excited state. The atom in the ground state absorbs some energy and goes to the excited state. Some atomic systems such as chromium neon etc. posses metastable states.

questions.question_hindi: प्रकाश विद्युत परिणाम प्रयोग में विगलन ऊपर वाली आवृत्ति में निष्कासित किये गये इलेक्ट्रान की संख्या इससे समानुपाती होती है
options_english: the frequency of the incident light
questions.explanation_english: The photoelectric effect is the phenomenon where electrons are emitted from a material when it is exposed to light.  The photoelectric effect does not occur at all if the frequency of the light source is below a certain value. This value which is characteristic of the kind of metal surface used in the experiment, is called cutoff frequency. Above the cutoff frequency each photon of light carries, sufficient energy to eject an electron. Since each photon can eject one electron, increasing the intensity of light increases the number of photon reaching the material's surface and consequently increases the number of electrons ejected. So, the number of electron ejected in the photoelectric effect is directly proportional to the intensity of light.

questions.question_english: Thermocouple consists of
questions.question_hindi: तापयुग्म में होता है
questions.explanation_english: A thermocouple is a temperature sensor that operates based on the principle of the seebeck effect. It is a device composed of two dissimilar metal wires or conductors that are joined together at one end to form a junction. The other ends of the wires are typically connected to a measuring instrument or a control system.  When there is a temperature difference between the two junctions of a thermocouple, it generates a voltage known as the thermoelectric voltage. It is directly proportional to the temperature difference between the two junctions. By measuring this voltage, the temperature at one of the junctions (known as measurement or hot junction) can be inferred relative to the temperature at the other junction (known as the reference of cold junction).

questions.question_hindi: अतिचालकों को जब ऊण् के नीचे ठंडा किया जाता है तब वे निम्न स्थिति में परिवर्तित हो जाते हैं
questions.explanation_english: A superconductors is defined as a substance that offers no resistance to the electric current when it becomes colder than a critical temperature. For example – aluminum, copper oxide, magnesium diboride etc.  When a superconductor is cooled below its critical temperature, it forms cooper pairs - a quantum mechanical phenomenon involving pairs of electrons with opposite momentum and spin. These cooper pairs in addition to zero electrical resistance also generate a perfect cancellation of any external magnetic field within the superconductors. questions.explanation_english: In superconductors, the energy gap is primarily due to interaction between electron and lattice vibrations which are known as phonons. This interaction is referred to as the electron phonon interaction. These interactions lead to the formation of pairs of electrons called cooper pairs with opposite momentum and spin.  The energy gap in a superconductor refers to the energy difference between the highest filled electron state (located below the gap) and the lowest available empty state (located above the gap) in the superconducting energy spectrum.  This energy gap is a characteristic feature of superconductors and is responsible for their unique properties such as zero electrical resistance and the expulsion of magnetic fields (Meissner effect).

This feature (negative resistance) makes it useful in oscillator and microwave amplifier applications.  Tunnel diodes are constructed with germanium or gallium arsenide by doping the p and n regions much more heavily than in a conventional rectifier diode. This is the negative resistance region.

questions.explanation_english: Beta decay is a form of radioactive decay that occurs when a nucleus emits a beta particle, which is either an electron or a position. It occurs when there is an imbalance between the number of neutrons and protons in the nucleus of an atom. Then nucleus becomes unstable and emits a beta particle to regain stability.  Beta decay conserves iso-spain, Baryon number and charge.  Parity refers to the concept of spatial symmetry. It describes whether a system remains unchanged under spatial inversion. Which is the transformation of coordinates from (x, y, z) to (-x, -y, -z). While parity is conserved in many fundamental interactions such as electromagnetic interaction, it is not conserved in weak interactions which are responsible for certain types of particle decay (β).

questions.question_english: At room temperature, the current in an intrinsic semiconductor is due to
questions.question_hindi: कमरे का तापमान पर आन्तरिक अर्धचालक में होने वाले करेंट का कारण है
questions.explanation_english: Intrinsic Semiconductor – A semiconductor in an extremely pure form is known as intrinsic semiconductor. In an intrinsic semiconductor, even at rooms temperature, hole-electron pairs are created. When electric field is applied across an intrinsic semiconductor, the current conduction takes place by two processes namely by free electrons and holes.  The free electrons are produced due to the breaking up of some covalent bonds by thermal energy. At the same time holes are created in the covalent bonds. Under the influence of electric field, conduction through the semiconductor is by both free electrons and holes. Therefore, the total current inside the semiconductor is the sum of currents due to free electrons and holes.

questions.explanation_english: A Geiger Muller counter is a device used for the detection and measurement of ionizing radiation.  When ionizing radiation enters the GM tube, it ionizes gas atoms or molecules within the tube creating free charge carriers (positive ions and electrons). These free charge carriers are then accelerated by a high voltage applied across the detector, leading to further ionization events and the creation of more charge carriers. This process results in a detectable electrical pulse or discharge, which is recorded and used to determine the presence and intensity of the radiation.
